svg.font-family: Amazon Ember, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: S3 change-data staging reference application — numbered flow
svg.desc: An eight-step flow. Step one is manual and is what starts everything: after deploying the destination stack, you call the subscription API with that stack's bucket and queue ARNs, which tells the Amazon Marketing Stream delivery service where to deliver. Band one, created by destination.yaml: Stream writes Parquet objects into an S3 delivery bucket, which posts a notification to an SQS queue. Band two, created by staging.yaml: the ingest job drains the queue and records each delivered file in an ingest manifest, reading only the files' Parquet footers and copying no rows; the merge job reads the files the manifest names for a window of arrival dates and resolves versions into a current-state table holding one row per record; and the aggregate job rebuilds summary tables for each declared grain. The tables drawn here — the ingest manifest, the current-state table and the summary tables — are Iceberg tables in one S3 Tables bucket, which also holds the other ingest-namespace tables the jobs maintain. Band three: Athena queries any of them, and QuickSight optionally reads them through Athena. Ingest is woken by an object-arrival event, with a schedule underneath as the floor and the only retry path. A numbered legend below the diagram describes each step.
svg.text: Eight steps, subscription to dashboard. Solid lines carry data; dashed lines are triggers, inputs and optional paths.
AWS Cloud — your account, one region
Deploy this stack first, subscribe against
its outputs, then deploy stack 2. There is
no import between the two, on purpose.
STACK 2 · staging.yaml — three Glue jobs, three Iceberg tables
a schedule underneath is the floor,
rebuilt by event date, never patched
Sample queries ship in queries/ for both
fine and coarse grain, and Athena can read
any of the three tables above directly.
All three live in one S3 Tables bucket.
Call the subscription API with stack 1's bucket and queue ARNs. By hand — no template can.
Stream then writes Parquet objects into the delivery bucket.
The bucket posts one notification per batch to the queue.
ingest drains the queue and records each delivered file in the manifest.
merge reads the files the manifest names and resolves versions — highest wins.
aggregate rebuilds the summary tables for every declared grain.
Athena queries any of the three tables. Nothing is copied out.
QuickSight reads them through Athena. Optional, and dashed throughout.
Steps 5 and 6 recompute rather than patch: a correction has no delta to apply.
